materials.text:
# Year 7 Humanities: course syllabus, 2026–27

Oakfield Middle School (fictional). Period 3 Humanities. Teacher: Ms J. Harrow (fictional).
Every name, date and policy in this document is invented for the Throughline demo.

## What this course is for

By the end of the year, students should be able to:

- Explain how geography shaped where and how the first civilisations grew.
- Read a primary source and say who made it, when, and what it was for.
- Build an argument from evidence, in discussion and in writing, and change their mind when the evidence says so.
- Write a clear paragraph with a claim, two pieces of evidence, and a sentence that ties them together.
- Work in a group so that everyone in it gets to speak.

## How the grade is calculated

| Category | Weight |
|---|---|
| Homework | 20% |
| Quizzes | 20% |
| Projects | 30% |
| Tests | 30% |

Homework is marked for completion and effort. Quizzes are short, every two weeks or so, and the lowest quiz score is dropped at the end of each term. Projects are the big pieces (the timeline, the city-state podcast, the DBQ essay) and come with a rubric. Tests close each unit.

## Units

1. The Fertile Crescent and the first cities (September to mid-October)
2. Hammurabi, law and fairness (mid-October to November)
3. Egypt and the Nile (December to January)
4. Greece: city-states, democracy and the Persian wars (February to March)
5. Rome from republic to empire (April to May)
6. Choice project and exhibition (June)

## Policies

- Late homework is accepted for full credit up to one week late; after that it is half credit until the end of the term.
- Any quiz can be retaken once within two weeks for the higher score.
- A missed test is made up during the next lunch slot; a missed project deadline is discussed with the student first.
- Phones stay in bags during class. First reminder is free; the second means the phone goes on the desk at the front.
- Work handed in must be the student's own; a source used must be named.
- Families can expect an email in the first week of each unit with what we are reading and when the test is.

Questions are welcome any time: catch me before school or email through the office.

json.overview:
Rowan started the year loud. On 2 September he talked through the whole map introduction and was moved twice; the note calls it "not rude, just constant." A new seat next to Ember helped within the week. Early grades were low against the class: the Summer Reading Reflection at 60% (class mean 87%), the Fertile Crescent Map at 65% and Quiz 1 at 60%. Behaviour stayed uneven through September. He turned one moment into a stand-up routine on 18 September, and on 22 September he was sent out for throwing a rubber at Alex. He came back and apologised without being asked, which the note marks as new.

The turn came with argument. In the Hammurabi introduction on 14 September he argued the eye-for-an-eye question well and listened. He asked to be prosecution lead for the Hammurabi Trial and objected to everything, but in role. The trial scored 97% (class mean 89%), and the note says he lost "graciously (mostly)." From there the scores climbed: Unit 1 Test 83%, Quiz 3 80%, and on 19 October a presentation at 93% that was "funny, accurate, kept to time." He has been nominated for the humanities showcase with Ember. The grade summary shows the overall at 78% and rising, from 68% over the first half of the scores to 84% over the second.

The thread is that his energy for talk became an asset once it had a structure: a role, a side to argue, a time limit. Homework (70%) and quizzes (72%) remain his weaker categories. The unit test note says he ran out of time on the essay. There are no notes after 19 October, and nothing yet on his paragraph writing or on group work.

He missed the Timeline Project deadline on 25 September but handed it in late, with dates in the right order and a picture of the stele. It still needed captions, and it scored 80%. Early October brought two notes: on 7 October he noticed something and handed it over, which the note says would not have happened a month earlier, and on 8 October he came to something and stayed the whole 40 minutes.

On 14 October he scored 31/40 (78%) on the Unit 1 Test and wrote 'proud of this' on it. The grade summary shows an overall 66%, rising from 48% over the first half of scores to 73% over the second. His later scores (75% on Quiz 3 and 73% on the Cuneiform Presentation) are steadier but still below the class means. The thread running through the period is organisation: as the systems around him took hold, the work started arriving and the scores rose. There are no notes after 14 October.

json.overview:
Ember started the year strongly. In the first week her paragraph on why rivers mattered had a clear claim and two pieces of evidence without prompting, and you thought of sharing it as a model. Her September homework scores were all 90% or above, well over the class means. She asked to do the extension reading on Sumerian schools, and her group finished early on 21 September. Early seating notes show her sitting next to a classmate who tends to distract, ignoring him until he gave up.

The Hammurabi trial at the end of September and start of October was the high point. She was annoyed for about a minute at being given the defence rather than prosecution, then started planning her case. Her closing argument got applause, and the trial scored 30/30. In the week before the Unit 1 Test she ran a review table without being asked, then scored 39/40, losing the one mark on spelling Euphrates. Her last recorded grade, the Cuneiform Presentation on 19 October, was 27/30 (90%), level with the class mean. It is the only grade not above the mean. Around then she said a classmate's work was better than hers.

She stands at 96% overall. The grade trend is steady, 96% over the first half of the scores and 95% over the second. The thread through the notes is initiative: extension reading, running ahead, running a review table. She is also prepared, with page numbers ready in discussion. There are no notes after 19 October, so the current Hammurabi unit into November is not covered.
